layer-boundary.title: SMT101: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.
layer-boundary.description: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist. Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.imports.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain. Repair: Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.
layer-boundary.markdownDescription:
**SMT101 — layer-boundary**

A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.

Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.imports.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import SqlVoiceSessionRepository
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.ports import VoiceSessionRepository

# gateway/bootstrap.py wires SqlVoiceSessionRepository to the port
```

Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain layer-boundary` for details.

cross-feature-import.title: SMT102: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.
cross-feature-import.description: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs. Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.imports.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence. Repair: Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.
cross-feature-import.markdownDescription:
**SMT102 — cross-feature-import**

A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.

Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.imports.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/infra/charges.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import CallLog
```

**Preferred**
```python
# billing/application/charges.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.api import CallSummaryQuery
```

Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.

Run `smelt explain cross-feature-import` for details.

third-party-denied.title: SMT103: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.
third-party-denied.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.imports.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed. Repair: Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.
third-party-denied.markdownDescription:
**SMT103 — third-party-denied**

A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.

Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.imports.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/domain/session.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/domain/session.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
```

Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.

Run `smelt explain third-party-denied` for details.

import-cycle.title: SMT104: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.
import-cycle.description: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.
import-cycle.markdownDescription:
**SMT104 — import-cycle**

Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.

Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/application/invoices.py
from gateway.features.voice.application import calls
# voice/application/calls.py
from gateway.features.billing.application import invoices
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/calls.py publishes an event;
# billing/application/invoices.py subscribes to it.
```

Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.

Run `smelt explain import-cycle` for details.

shared-imports-feature.title: SMT105: A `shared` module or a central module (`architecture.modules`) imports a feature module.
shared-imports-feature.description: A `shared` module or a central module (`architecture.modules`) imports a feature module. Shared code and central layers such as a platform package are importable by every feature. If they depend on a feature, every feature transitively depends on that feature and the slices collapse. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project helpers and facades are checked and reported with a shortest import chain. Repair: Move the needed concept into shared, or move the shared code into the feature.
shared-imports-feature.markdownDescription:
**SMT105 — shared-imports-feature**

A `shared` module or a central module (`architecture.modules`) imports a feature module.

Shared code and central layers such as a platform package are importable by every feature. If they depend on a feature, every feature transitively depends on that feature and the slices collapse. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project helpers and facades are checked and reported with a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# gateway/shared/money.py
from gateway.features.billing.domain import Currency
```

**Preferred**
```python
# gateway/shared/money.py
class Currency: ...
```

Move the needed concept into shared, or move the shared code into the feature.

Run `smelt explain shared-imports-feature` for details.

composition-root-leak.title: SMT106: A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module.
composition-root-leak.description: A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module. Wiring belongs in one place. When features reach for the container or the bootstrap module, construction logic spreads and dependencies become hidden. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project modules are checked and reported with a shortest import chain. Repair: Receive dependencies through constructor parameters and register them in the composition root.
composition-root-leak.markdownDescription:
**SMT106 — composition-root-leak**

A module imports the composition root or a declared wiring module.

Wiring belongs in one place. When features reach for the container or the bootstrap module, construction logic spreads and dependencies become hidden. With architecture.imports.transitive, paths through arbitrary project modules are checked and reported with a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.main import container
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
class StartSession:
    def __init__(self, sessions: VoiceSessionRepository) -> None: ...
```

Receive dependencies through constructor parameters and register them in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain composition-root-leak` for details.

private-module-import.title: SMT107: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.
private-module-import.description: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module. Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Layer and feature policies apply independently. Repair: Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.
private-module-import.markdownDescription:
**SMT107 — private-module-import**

Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.

Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Layer and feature policies apply independently.

**Problem**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.orders.storage import OrderStore
```

**Preferred**
```python
# app/client.py
from app.orders.api import place_order
```

Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.

Run `smelt explain private-module-import` for details.

package-import-fanout.title: SMT108: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths.
package-import-fanout.description: One caller spreads a package API across several import paths. Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, including its facade when mixed with implementation imports, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository. Findings include missing static exports and a cycle witness for the proposed caller/facade edges. Known cycles block bundling advice. No-cycle-found covers only explicit runtime imports; dynamic imports and implicit package initialization remain unproven. Repair: Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Use proposed_exports to review missing re-exports. A cycle_check of cycle blocks bundling: keep the imports or resolve dependency direction first. No automatic rewrite is performed. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.
package-import-fanout.markdownDescription:
**SMT108 — package-import-fanout**

One caller spreads a package API across several import paths.

Repeated imports of neighboring implementation modules can indicate a missing package API. This is an opt-in design hint, not proof of poor architecture. Count distinct target modules per source file and contracted package, including its facade when mixed with implementation imports, not statements, symbols, or imports across the whole repository. Findings include missing static exports and a cycle witness for the proposed caller/facade edges. Known cycles block bundling advice. No-cycle-found covers only explicit runtime imports; dynamic imports and implicit package initialization remain unproven.

**Problem**
```python
# caller.py
from app.users.application.get_user import GetUser
from app.users.application.update_user import UpdateUser
from app.users.application.delete_user import DeleteUser
```

**Preferred**
```python
# caller.py, after deliberate facade exports are defined
from app.users.application import DeleteUser, GetUser, UpdateUser
```

Consider exporting the caller's supported API from the package facade. Use proposed_exports to review missing re-exports. A cycle_check of cycle blocks bundling: keep the imports or resolve dependency direction first. No automatic rewrite is performed. If these independent dependencies are intentional, retain them or adjust the advisory threshold. Declare public: ['.'] to enforce facade-only imports.

Run `smelt explain package-import-fanout` for details.

facade-export-gap.title: SMT109: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.
facade-export-gap.description: A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export. A contract's export_at threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional structure.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before. Repair: Review whether the name belongs in the package API or whether callers should move. The finding lists importers and other public export paths. A cycle witness means adding the facade dependency closes a runtime import path; no-cycle-found means only that no return path was found in the analyzed explicit module graph, not that initialization is safe. Dynamic imports, implicit package initialization and import order are not proven. No exports, imports or policy are rewritten automatically.
facade-export-gap.markdownDescription:
**SMT109 — facade-export-gap**

A public implementation name has many outside importers but no package export.

A contract's export_at threshold counts distinct analyzed modules outside the defining package, aggregating aliases and static re-export chains. One advisory finding per symbol and facade is anchored at the definition. Tests count only with count_tests: true; TYPE_CHECKING-only imports never count. Private names, module imports, namespace packages, uncertain bindings and recognized dynamic facade exports are skipped. Existing package exports and explicit __all__ re-exports in other modules are context, not coverage for this facade. Frequency suggests an API review, not a requirement to expand the public API. Counts cover analyzed code only. Optional structure.canonical_exports maps a qualified definition or static alias to its supported public export. Smelt verifies both against the same static identity, including supported literal lazy-export tables; missing, conflicting or unsupported dynamic owners are configuration errors. A verified owner prevents duplicate export advice for that symbol only. Importer context separates same-root and other-root production consumers. Ownership never relaxes layers, package-public contracts or cycle checks; without declarations existing thresholds behave as before.

**Problem**
```python
# app/browser/__init__.py is empty
# Three outside modules each use:
from app.browser.base import BrowserEvents
```

**Preferred**
```python
# After reviewing ownership and initialization behavior:
# app/browser/__init__.py
from .base import BrowserEvents
__all__ = ['BrowserEvents']
# callers
from app.browser import BrowserEvents
```

Review whether the name belongs in the package API or whether callers should move. The finding lists importers and other public export paths. A cycle witness means adding the facade dependency closes a runtime import path; no-cycle-found means only that no return path was found in the analyzed explicit module graph, not that initialization is safe. Dynamic imports, implicit package initialization and import order are not proven. No exports, imports or policy are rewritten automatically.

Run `smelt explain facade-export-gap` for details.

unknown-layer.title: SMT301: A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers.
unknown-layer.description: A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers. Code outside the layer grid is invisible to every layer rule: voice/models/ or voice/helpers.py can import anything and be imported by anything. A feature's __init__.py is fine, and not every feature needs every layer. Repair: Move the code into a declared layer, or declare its package as a layer if the architecture has a distinct responsibility for it.
unknown-layer.markdownDescription:
**SMT301 — unknown-layer**

A feature contains a package or module outside the declared layers.

Code outside the layer grid is invisible to every layer rule: voice/models/ or voice/helpers.py can import anything and be imported by anything. A feature's __init__.py is fine, and not every feature needs every layer.

**Problem**
```python
voice/
  domain/
  application/
  models/      # not a layer
  helpers.py   # in no layer
```

**Preferred**
```python
voice/
  domain/
    models.py
  application/
```

Move the code into a declared layer, or declare its package as a layer if the architecture has a distinct responsibility for it.

Run `smelt explain unknown-layer` for details.

forbidden-package-name.title: SMT302: A package or module name is listed in structure.forbidden_names.
forbidden-package-name.description: A package or module name is listed in structure.forbidden_names. Names like utils or helpers describe nothing, so everything fits in them. They grow into grab bags that every layer imports. Repair: Name the module after what it does, or move each function next to its callers.
forbidden-package-name.markdownDescription:
**SMT302 — forbidden-package-name**

A package or module name is listed in structure.forbidden_names.

Names like utils or helpers describe nothing, so everything fits in them. They grow into grab bags that every layer imports.

**Problem**
```python
voice/application/utils.py
```

**Preferred**
```python
voice/application/durations.py
```

Name the module after what it does, or move each function next to its callers.

Run `smelt explain forbidden-package-name` for details.

unclassified-module.title: SMT305: A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root.
unclassified-module.description: A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root. Unclassified modules are exempt from layer and feature boundary checks: a domain module may import them. Composition-root/wiring restrictions and configured cycle checks still apply. Central code such as a database or storage package belongs to a layer via architecture.modules. Root packages with no classified module at all (libraries) are skipped. Repair: Give the package a layer under architecture.modules, list it in architecture.shared or composition_root, or move it into a feature.
unclassified-module.markdownDescription:
**SMT305 — unclassified-module**

A module maps to no feature, layer, shared set or composition root.

Unclassified modules are exempt from layer and feature boundary checks: a domain module may import them. Composition-root/wiring restrictions and configured cycle checks still apply. Central code such as a database or storage package belongs to a layer via architecture.modules. Root packages with no classified module at all (libraries) are skipped.

**Problem**
```python
gateway/
  platform/db.py    # neither shared, a layer nor a feature
```

**Preferred**
```python
# smelt.yml
architecture:
  modules:
    gateway.platform: infrastructure
```

Give the package a layer under architecture.modules, list it in architecture.shared or composition_root, or move it into a feature.

Run `smelt explain unclassified-module` for details.

incomplete-coverage.title: SMT306: Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason.
incomplete-coverage.description: Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason. A passing architecture check is only useful when production code cannot silently escape its package selection or classification. Strict coverage inventories source roots and Python workspace members independently of project.root_packages. Pure package facades do not need their own layer. Repair: Select missing production packages and assign their architecture role. Move unclassified implementation into an existing layer. Deliberately excluded code needs project.exclude entries with path and reason. Coverage gaps cannot be hidden by debt, inline ignores or a narrowed check.
incomplete-coverage.markdownDescription:
**SMT306 — incomplete-coverage**

Strict coverage found source outside the architecture policy or an exclusion without a reason.

A passing architecture check is only useful when production code cannot silently escape its package selection or classification. Strict coverage inventories source roots and Python workspace members independently of project.root_packages. Pure package facades do not need their own layer.

**Problem**
```yaml
# smelt.yml
project:
  root_packages: [backend]
  coverage: strict
# A new workspace library exists but is not selected or classified.
```

**Preferred**
```yaml
# smelt.yml
project:
  root_packages: [backend, client]
  source_roots: [backend/src, libs/client/src]
  coverage: strict
architecture:
  modules: {client: infrastructure}
```

import-style.title: SMT308: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style.
import-style.description: An import does not follow the package's declared relative/absolute style. A predictable import style makes ownership easier to read. The closest package contract supplies the style. No style is enforced without an explicit contract, and this rule never changes bindings. Repair: Use a relative import within the configured dot limit, otherwise use an absolute import. Preserve aliases and update references if converting an import statement changes its binding. forbidden-future-annotations.title: SMT310: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy.
forbidden-future-annotations.description: The annotations future import violates a package or Python-version policy. An explicit source convention can forbid this import. unnecessary-future-annotations.title: SMT311: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need.
unnecessary-future-annotations.description: Review an annotations future import with no detected postponement need. On targets before Python 3.14 or with an unknown minimum, when-needed mode retains imports for quoted and unresolved forward references, TYPE_CHECKING, runtime annotation inspection, decorated definitions and complex annotation expressions. This includes dataclasses and Pydantic models: decoration can consume annotations, so modern decorated code may receive no hint even when removal happens to work. Other cases get a conservative review hint, not proof of safe removal. Declared Python 3.14+ targets are handled by SMT310. Repair: Review whether postponement is part of the module's runtime contract, then remove unnecessary boilerplate and verify types and behavior. On Python 3.12/3.13, an annotations future import is appropriate when the chosen public-first order uses forward references; SMT313 preserves eager dependencies when the import is absent. Keep the import if it serves a real purpose; annotate a justified exception if required. Self is only an alternative for methods whose return contract follows the receiver's subclass, such as returning self or constructing cls; a matching class-name annotation alone is insufficient. No Self rewrite is suggested automatically.

no-private-modules.title: SMT312: A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy.
no-private-modules.description: A module or package has an underscore prefix forbidden by its naming policy. Some projects use descriptive module names and keep private helpers inside them. This opt-in naming convention rejects _service.py and _internal/ even when they export public symbols. __init__.py and __main__.py retain their Python-defined roles. Repair: Choose a descriptive module or package name without a leading underscore, then update imports and deliberate facade exports. A more specific package can explicitly allow the convention. No files or symbols are renamed automatically.

public-definitions-first.title: SMT313: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries.
public-definitions-first.description: Definitions are out of public-first order within modeled execution boundaries. Public interfaces should be easy to find. A stable topological order prioritizes configured categories while preserving category order, definition-time reads, rebinding and execution barriers. Function bodies are deferred; decorators, defaults, assignments and eager annotations are not. Future imports and declared Python 3.14+ targets defer annotations. Unions of recognized, unshadowed builtin types (and None) are modeled in eager function annotations for declared Python 3.10+ targets; imported or user-defined types and operator expressions in defaults remain unknown. Overload/property families remain atomic. Unknown execution is pinned. Attribute dictionaries of unambiguous undecorated nested functions are distinct from the enclosing ordered namespace, so vars(local_function) and local_function.__dict__ alone do not block enclosing moves. Nonlocal closure writes alone are also unrelated to module/class definition order. Unknown receivers, globals, locals, vars(), global writes and code/annotation introspection still require review. Repair: Review the expected order and execution barriers. Explicit check --fix can apply bounded moves where the package permits safe-only fixes. Imports, unknown execution and a misplaced main guard require manual review. Names and visibility are never rewritten by ordering. Refused sections identify the triggering expression and its source location in fix_blocker and fix_reason; the safety boundary stays in place. Pinned definitions are listed under coverage.ordering[].barriers with check --format json --show-coverage. Dependencies take precedence over public-first order. On Python 3.12/3.13, keep a needed annotations future import when the chosen order uses forward references; SMT311 retains it.

bundled-instance-assignment.title: SMT314: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.
bundled-instance-assignment.description: An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention. Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error. Repair: Use one direct instance attribute write per statement. Preserve evaluation timing: unpack computed values into locals before assigning fields when appropriate. Parallel assignments, swaps, descriptors and unpacking failures can behave differently when split, so there is no automatic rewrite.
bundled-instance-assignment.markdownDescription:
**SMT314 — bundled-instance-assignment**

An assignment writes multiple direct instance attributes under a separate-assignment convention.

Separate field assignments make object initialization easy to scan and extend. This opt-in package convention reports tuple/list unpacking and chained assignments that write multiple direct attributes of a method's first positional parameter, regardless of its name. It leaves local unpacking and single-field assignments alone. Recognized static/class methods and nested helper bodies are excluded; nested classes are inspected with their own receiver. This is a readability policy, not a logic error.

**Problem**
```python

    def __init__(self, log, control):
        self.log, self.control = log, control
```

**Preferred**

prefer-match-type-dispatch.title: SMT315: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.
prefer-match-type-dispatch.description: Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy. Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior. Repair: Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.
prefer-match-type-dispatch.markdownDescription:
**SMT315 — prefer-match-type-dispatch**

Review a same-subject isinstance/elif chain for match/case under an explicit package policy.

Long type-dispatch chains can be clearer as class patterns and guards. This opt-in hint recognizes positive builtin isinstance tests over the same simple name, optionally followed by and guards. It preserves independent adjacent if statements and reports one candidate per whole supported chain. It is a readability suggestion, not proof of equivalent class-pattern behavior.

**Problem**
```python
if isinstance(event, Started):
    start(event)
elif isinstance(event, Delta | Progress):
    update(event)
elif isinstance(event, Finished) and event.ok:
    finish(event)
```

**Preferred**
```python
match event:
    case Started():
        start(event)
    case Delta() | Progress():
        update(event)
    case Finished() if event.ok:
        finish(event)
```

Review class patterns, guards and subclass ordering. Preserve independent if statements, and keep nested body conditions inside their case: moving them into a case guard can introduce fallthrough. Match evaluates its subject once; custom instance checks, dynamic type expressions and side effects may differ. No automatic rewrite is performed. Declared Python minima before 3.10 are excluded; unknown minima require version review.

Run `smelt explain prefer-match-type-dispatch` for details.

internal-public-member.title: SMT316: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class.
internal-public-member.description: A public module function or instance method has no observed use outside its module or class. An implementation helper should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in package review includes unused definitions and internally used sync/async functions and ordinary instance methods. Imports and module escapes preserve module functions; known test accesses also count as external use, leaving test-only public functions to SMT429. Explicit module __all__ exports and decorated functions are preserved. Methods on decorated, inherited or subclassed classes, special/private methods, properties and class/static methods are excluded. For methods, even unresolved same-named attribute accesses outside the owning class conservatively preserve visibility. External libraries, frameworks, dynamic reflection and unscanned callers cannot be ruled out. This finding asks for review and does not prove a rename is safe. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings preserve their public methods, including aliased re-export chains. Export evidence participates in incremental cache invalidation. Literal lazy-export tables are recognized only with a matching guarded importlib.import_module/getattr forwarder and optional globals cache. The table may supply __all__ through sorted/list/tuple. Arbitrary __getattr__, mutated/escaped tables and stubs alone do not verify runtime exports. Repair: Review the supported interface and callers. For a genuine internal helper, add a leading underscore and update calls and callback references. Resolve existing private-name collisions before renaming. Preserve deliberate public APIs with __all__ for module functions or append `# smelt: ignore[SMT316] -- <specific API reason>` to the reported definition. Keep the concrete reason beside the code; Smelt cannot verify its truth. No automatic rename is performed.

internal-static-helper.title: SMT317: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function.
internal-static-helper.description: An internal static helper can be reviewed for extraction to a private module function. A helper that needs neither instance nor class state is often easier to find and reuse as a private module function. This package convention reviews direct sync/async methods carrying only the recognized builtin staticmethod decorator, including import aliases. Known or unresolved external same-named attribute access preserves static APIs. Classes with inheritance, subclasses or decorators, additional method decorators, special methods, __class__/super references and detected class-namespace dependencies are excluded. This is a placement preference, not proof of equivalent runtime behavior; external/dynamic consumers and definition-time dependencies still need review. Excluded files, unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed; findings expose usage_scope so absence of observed callers is not mistaken for a whole-project proof. Repair: Move the helper to module scope with a leading underscore, remove @staticmethod, and update class/instance-qualified calls and callback references. Preserve annotations, defaults, evaluation order and dependencies; choose a distinct name if the module already binds it. Keep deliberate static APIs with a closest package rule set to off or reasoned suppression. No automatic extraction is performed.

redundant-str-enum-value.title: SMT318: Review .value on a known StrEnum member for direct use of the member.
redundant-str-enum-value.description: Review .value on a known StrEnum member for direct use of the member. StrEnum members are already strings, so extracting .value often adds noise and loses the enum type unnecessarily. This opt-in hint recognizes direct Class.MEMBER.value reads on analyzed, top-level classes inheriting directly from enum.StrEnum, including import aliases, relative imports and analyzed re-exports. Simple string, auto() and member-alias declarations are supported. Ordinary Enum, str/Enum mixins, unknown or shadowed bindings, custom enum construction/value access, instance variables and dynamic lookups are excluded. Shadowing anywhere in a module conservatively limits recognition there. Repair: Prefer the member directly when the consumer accepts string subclasses. Review boundary behavior first: exact str checks, identity, repr and serialization contracts can distinguish the member from its raw value. Literal-typed parameters can also reject the member in a type checker; Smelt has no consumer type information. Keep .value or an explicit str(member) conversion where a plain string is intentional, and suppress the hint with a reason. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.

prefer-package-import.description: Prefer an existing package re-export over an implementation import. This opt-in hint requires every name in a from-import to have an unconditional, direct, same-named public re-export in an analyzed ancestor __init__.py. The nearest eligible package is suggested. Static __all__ is respected. Imports inside that package are excluded to avoid routing its own implementation through its initializer. Imports in package initializers also stay unchanged. Conditional, rebound, private, star and dynamic exports, re-export chains, module imports and unscanned third-party packages are outside this check. Repair: Use the suggested package import and combine it with an existing import there when both are in the same scope and guard. Preserve aliases, comments and relative/absolute import policy. Review initializer side effects and dependency cycles. No exports are created and no automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed.

implicit-optional-default.title: SMT321: An optional parameter with a None default uses truthiness to choose a fallback.
implicit-optional-default.description: An optional parameter with a None default uses truthiness to choose a fallback. For an explicitly optional parameter, None commonly means not supplied. Using parameter or fallback also replaces valid falsy values such as zero, empty strings, empty containers and objects with custom truthiness. This opt-in review recognizes two-operand or expressions whose first operand is a directly named, unrebound parameter with a literal None default and a syntactic optional annotation (including quoted unions and typing Optional/Union/Annotated). It skips nested scopes, boolean tests, and parameters rebound anywhere in their function. Intentional falsy defaults remain valid; suppress or disable the review there. This is bounded syntax analysis, not type or control-flow inference. Repair: Review whether only None should select the fallback. If so, use parameter if parameter is not None else fallback. smelt check --select SMT321 --fix --unsafe-fixes applies this behavior-changing rewrite only to visible findings. Plain --fix leaves it unchanged. The rewrite preserves fallback laziness and source outside each expression; inline comments or explicit line continuations within an expression require manual editing. Intentional truthiness fallback should remain unchanged. Debt and changed comparisons distinguish enclosing functions, including class and nested-function names. Older debt without a function identity requires review and explicit re-recording; debt --prune does not accept it under a new function.
implicit-optional-default.markdownDescription:
**SMT321 — implicit-optional-default**

An optional parameter with a None default uses truthiness to choose a fallback.

For an explicitly optional parameter, None commonly means not supplied. Using parameter or fallback also replaces valid falsy values such as zero, empty strings, empty containers and objects with custom truthiness. This opt-in review recognizes two-operand or expressions whose first operand is a directly named, unrebound parameter with a literal None default and a syntactic optional annotation (including quoted unions and typing Optional/Union/Annotated). It skips nested scopes, boolean tests, and parameters rebound anywhere in their function. Intentional falsy defaults remain valid; suppress or disable the review there. This is bounded syntax analysis, not type or control-flow inference.

**Problem**
```python
def create(options: Options | None = None):
    self.options = options or Options()
```

**Preferred**
```python
def create(options: Options | None = None):
    self.options = options if options is not None else Options()
```

If so, use parameter if parameter is not None else fallback. smelt check --select SMT321 --fix --unsafe-fixes applies this behavior-changing rewrite only to visible findings. Plain --fix leaves it unchanged. The rewrite preserves fallback laziness and source outside each expression; inline comments or explicit line continuations within an expression require manual editing. Intentional truthiness fallback should remain unchanged. Debt and changed comparisons distinguish enclosing functions, including class and nested-function names. Older debt without a function identity requires review and explicit re-recording; debt --prune does not accept it under a new function.

deep-object-navigation.title: SMT322: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes.
deep-object-navigation.description: Review a method call reached through multiple instance attributes. An instance method that reaches through several stored collaborators depends on their internal arrangement. This opt-in Law of Demeter review reports calls with at least two consecutive attribute accesses from the instance receiver before the first method call, such as self.browser.input.motor(). One finding covers a whole receiver call chain. Direct collaborator calls, pure data reads and fluent chains starting from a direct collaborator are excluded. Module objects stored from unshadowed imports or declared as ModuleType, explicit SimpleNamespace trees, and typed dataclass/Pydantic record paths ending in known containers or values are namespaces rather than collaborator graphs. Known pathlib parent paths and subprocess pipes also retain their standard APIs. Namespace evidence comes from annotations, direct constructor assignments and property return annotations; analyzed imports and re-exports are followed without executing code. Every intermediate object must be a known namespace or value: a record containing a service does not exempt navigation into that service. Names such as api, client, get or append alone exempt nothing. Unknown SDK types and dynamic property/data flow remain review limitations. Decorated and implicit class/static methods, nested helper bodies, comprehensions, receiver rebinding and navigation through parameters, aliases or subscripts are outside the review. This is a bounded review, not proof of a design defect. When namespace evidence is incomplete, the finding includes the declared/constructed root type and the unresolved step. These are review inputs for an agent, not proof that the API is poorly designed. Inspect the public API contract before choosing a refactor; an intentional namespace can be a valid conclusion. Repair: Review whether the caller should receive the needed collaborator directly or ask its direct collaborator to perform the operation. A local variable alone does not reduce structural coupling. Preserve factory/property evaluation and object lifetimes; repeated lookups need not return the same object. Keep intentional API navigation with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned SMT322 suppression. No automatic rewrite is performed. Enable with rules: {deep-object-navigation: hint}, globally or in a package contract, or --select SMT322.

no-base-class-prefix.title: SMT323: A class definition uses the Base prefix forbidden by the selected naming convention.
no-base-class-prefix.description: A class definition uses the Base prefix forbidden by the selected naming convention. BaseService names a position in an inheritance hierarchy rather than the abstraction's responsibility. A responsibility-based name such as Service keeps that implementation choice out of the name. The prefix does not itself create additional dependency coupling, and inheritance can be intentional, so this is an opt-in naming convention rather than a correctness check or an inheritance ban. It checks all class definitions in matching production modules, including private, nested and local classes, without inferring whether they have subclasses. After leading underscores, Base must be the whole name or be followed by an uppercase letter or underscore. Baseline, Baseball and Base64 remain valid. Imports, aliases, function names and test files are outside scope; inheriting from an imported BaseModel is allowed. Repair: Choose a name describing the class's responsibility or contract, then update references and deliberate exports. Preserve inheritance where it serves the design. A more specific package rule can disable the convention for compatibility. No symbols are renamed automatically. Enable with rules: {no-base-class-prefix: error}, globally or in a package contract, or --select SMT323.

prefer-str-enum-discriminator.title: SMT324: Prefer StrEnum members for single-string class discriminator fields.
prefer-str-enum-discriminator.description: Prefer StrEnum members for single-string class discriminator fields. Discriminated union variants often repeat protocol strings in Literal annotations, field defaults and dispatch code. A shared StrEnum gives those values one named definition while Literal[EventType.MEMBER] preserves each variant's narrow type. This opt-in syntax review recognizes directly annotated class fields named type, kind or tag whose typing.Literal contains exactly one raw string, with or without a default. It supports typing and typing_extensions import aliases, quoted annotations and Annotated/Required/NotRequired wrappers. Dataclasses, model classes and class-based TypedDict declarations use the same syntax. The field shape is a review candidate, not proof of union membership. Other field names, multiple-value Literals, enum-member Literals, ClassVar, type aliases, inherited fields and uncertain or shadowed typing bindings are excluded. Declared Python minima before 3.11 are excluded; unknown minima require version review. Repair: Define or reuse a shared StrEnum for the union's wire values. Keep each variant annotated as Literal[EnumType.MEMBER], and use that same member in direct defaults, dataclasses.field(default=...) or model Field(default=...). Keep explicit string values such as checkpoint.extension; auto() may change the wire contract. Review consumers and serialization before changing defaults, since exact str checks and repr can distinguish enum members. StrEnum requires Python 3.11+. No automatic rewrite is performed; analyzed code is never executed. Suppress intentional external schema strings with a reason or disable this review for their package.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal
```

caller-before-callee.description: A direct caller appears after same-visibility helpers it calls. A step-down reading order introduces a higher-level operation before its lower-level helpers. It resolves direct same-module names and receiver.method calls, excludes shadowed bindings, nested scopes, comprehensions, dunder methods and recursive call components, and respects definition-time parameter/return dependencies. prefer-callable-instance.title: SMT333: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method.
prefer-callable-instance.description: Review __call__ and an operation-based class name for a single public method. A class with one public instance method can express its operation through __call__ and a class name describing that operation. This opt-in design review reports one candidate per plain class with exactly one directly declared public method. Private helpers and __init__ do not count as public operations. An existing __call__ is already a callable API and is never reported. Constructor and operation signatures are reported separately, including positional-only, keyword-only and variadic arguments: construction configures the object, while __call__ must retain the method's call-time arguments and async behavior. Classes with bases, metaclass keywords, class or method decorators, additional special methods, class-level data or conditional definitions are excluded. This keeps inherited APIs, descriptors, dataclasses and explicit protocols outside this bounded syntax review. Test files are excluded. A single method does not prove a design defect: published named APIs and stateful lifecycles can justify keeping the class as it is. Dynamic monkey-patching and external API consumers are not resolved. Repair: Consider renaming the sole public method to __call__ and naming the class after its operation (for example, ReportService.generate becomes GenerateReport.__call__). Preserve the constructor signature, call-time parameters, defaults, return annotations and async behavior; do not move constructor dependencies into __call__. Review callers, dependency injection registrations and public compatibility before changing either name. No names, arguments or callers are rewritten automatically. Enable rules: {prefer-callable-instance: hint}, globally or in a package contract, or --select SMT333. Keep an intentional named API with a package rules override set to off or a reasoned SMT333 suppression.

private-class-constant.title: SMT334: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module.
private-class-constant.description: A private literal constant is declared on an ordinary class instead of its module. Implementation constants such as a controller's supported file extensions belong beside the class as private module constants when they do not form part of its object contract. This opt-in convention reports private UPPER_CASE names assigned literal scalars or recursively literal sets, lists, tuples and dictionaries in production class bodies, including annotated, chained and guarded assignments. It checks nested and local classes independently. Classes with bases, decorators or class keywords are excluded conservatively because inheritance, enums, data models and metaclasses can give attributes a class-specific contract. Public names, lowercase fields, dunder names, instance assignments, method locals, calls, comprehensions and values referring to other names are outside scope. This is a placement convention; syntax alone cannot prove that callers never override or mutate an attribute. Repair: Move the constant to the same module with a leading underscore, then update class-qualified and instance-qualified reads to use the constant name directly. Check name collisions, initialization order, name mangling, mutation, subclass overrides and external consumers before moving it. Keep intentional class contracts with a reasoned suppression or package override. Enable rules: {private-class-constant: error} to block the convention, or --select SMT334 to review it. No automatic move or rewrite is performed.

internal-public-attribute.title: SMT335: A public instance or class data attribute has no observed access outside its class.
internal-public-attribute.description: A public instance or class data attribute has no observed access outside its class. Implementation state should not advertise a public interface solely because it lacks a leading underscore. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes, including unused attributes. Any same-named access outside the owning class conservatively preserves visibility, including unresolved receivers, writes, deletions and literal reflection. Test accesses count even when test-quality rules exclude the file; test-only reads remain the responsibility of SMT430, so these rules do not overlap. Private names, methods/properties, possible descriptors, decorated/inherited/subclassed classes, slots and custom attribute hooks are excluded. This also preserves dataclass, attrs, Pydantic, NamedTuple and TypedDict data contracts. Classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings retain their public attributes, including aliased re-export chains. test-location.title: SMT401: A test file does not live where tests.layout expects it.
test-location.description: A test file does not live where tests.layout expects it. A predictable test location lets readers and agents find the tests of a module, and a test whose mirrored source no longer exists is left over from a rename or move. With `layout: mirror` the path decides: tests/billing/test_invoice.py needs app/billing/invoice.py, a package test tests/billing/test_billing.py needs app/billing/. Not every module needs a test. tests.mirror sets the convention, relative to the test root. Repair: Move or rename the file so its path mirrors the module it tests, merge it into that module's test, or list deliberately unmirrored tests (behaviour, integration, e2e) in tests.unmirrored. A missing mirrored source says nothing about whether the tested behaviour exists. Imports through package facades count as imports of the defining module. A move is suggested only when the test imports its subject (or is named exactly after it, marked `evidence: name`); otherwise `expected.candidates` lists the imported modules with their names and mirrored test paths to choose from, and two imported modules of the test's name stay undecided.

A move_on_after scope or a configured timeout helper alone does not establish outcome evidence. Possibly swallowed helper assertions supply no evidence; known raising timeout contexts retain it. It neither proves assertions execute nor judges their strength; a frozen scheduler clock can also defeat a timeout. Positive validation/smoke tests can be intentional exceptions. test-only-public-function.description: A public module function is accessed from tests but has no observed production use outside its own module. Leaving an internal helper public just so tests can call it enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to implementation details. This opt-in review identifies undecorated top-level sync/async functions without a leading underscore, referenced by analyzed tests and not imported or accessed by another analyzed production module. Uses inside the defining module do not justify public visibility. Aliased/relative imports and analyzed re-exports are resolved; production imports, star imports and escaped module values conservatively preserve the API. Explicit __all__ exports, dynamic export declarations, decorated functions, rebound names, methods and nested functions are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence. External consumers, packaging entry points and arbitrary dynamic access are not fully known; a finding is a review candidate, not proof that a function can be made private safely. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), packages outside source selection and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent. Findings expose the configured usage_scope. When no references exist inside the defining module either, the finding says unused outside tests among analyzed modules and lists the internal reference evidence. This is not proof of dead code for unassessed consumers. Repair: If this is an internal helper, add a leading underscore and update internal references. Prefer testing the public behavior that calls it. If direct helper tests are deliberate, keep a reasoned private-access exception; if it is a supported external API, declare it in __all__ or document a reasoned suppression. Review callers before renaming.
test-only-public-function.markdownDescription:
**SMT429 — test-only-public-function**

A public module function is accessed from tests but has no observed production use outside its own module.

Leaving an internal helper public just so tests can call it enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to implementation details. This opt-in review identifies undecorated top-level sync/async functions without a leading underscore, referenced by analyzed tests and not imported or accessed by another analyzed production module. Uses inside the defining module do not justify public visibility. Aliased/relative imports and analyzed re-exports are resolved; production imports, star imports and escaped module values conservatively preserve the API. Explicit __all__ exports, dynamic export declarations, decorated functions, rebound names, methods and nested functions are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence. External consumers, packaging entry points and arbitrary dynamic access are not fully known; a finding is a review candidate, not proof that a function can be made private safely. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), packages outside source selection and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent. Findings expose the configured usage_scope. When no references exist inside the defining module either, the finding says unused outside tests among analyzed modules and lists the internal reference evidence. This is not proof of dead code for unassessed consumers.

**Problem**
```python
__all__ = ['drag']
async def drag_gesture(tab): ...
async def drag(tab):
    await drag_gesture(tab)
# tests/test_mouse.py
from app.mouse import drag_gesture
```

**Preferred**
```python
__all__ = ['drag']
async def _drag_gesture(tab): ...
async def drag(tab):
    await _drag_gesture(tab)
# tests/test_mouse.py
from app.mouse import drag
```

If this is an internal helper, add a leading underscore and update internal references. Prefer testing the public behavior that calls it. If direct helper tests are deliberate, keep a reasoned private-access exception; if it is a supported external API, declare it in __all__ or document a reasoned suppression. Review callers before renaming.

Run `smelt explain test-only-public-function` for details.

test-only-public-attribute.title: SMT430: A public attribute is read from tests but has no observed production access outside its class.
test-only-public-attribute.description: A public attribute is read from tests but has no observed production access outside its class. Exposing implementation state just for tests enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to internal representation. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes. Reads by analyzed tests are resolved through known constructors, annotations, fixtures and class aliases/re-exports. Internal class accesses do not justify public visibility. Any same-named production attribute access outside the owning class, including unresolved receivers and literal reflection, conservatively preserves visibility. Private names, methods/properties, descriptors, decorated/inherited/subclassed classes, slots and custom attribute hooks are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence; test writes alone do not trigger a finding. External consumers and arbitrary dynamic access remain unknown, so renaming requires review. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent; usage_scope records the configured analysis boundary. Public attributes of classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings are treated as supported API and retained, including aliased re-export chains. Repair: Review whether the attribute belongs to the supported API. For internal state, add a leading underscore, update class references and test observable public behavior. Keep deliberate external or framework contracts with a reasoned suppression. Suggested names avoid observed collisions; no automatic rename is performed.
test-only-public-attribute.markdownDescription:
**SMT430 — test-only-public-attribute**

A public attribute is read from tests but has no observed production access outside its class.

Exposing implementation state just for tests enlarges the apparent API and couples tests to internal representation. This opt-in review covers direct instance assignments in ordinary methods and simple class data declarations on unambiguous top-level classes. Reads by analyzed tests are resolved through known constructors, annotations, fixtures and class aliases/re-exports. Internal class accesses do not justify public visibility. Any same-named production attribute access outside the owning class, including unresolved receivers and literal reflection, conservatively preserves visibility. Private names, methods/properties, descriptors, decorated/inherited/subclassed classes, slots and custom attribute hooks are excluded. Test-quality exclusions apply to test evidence; test writes alone do not trigger a finding. External consumers and arbitrary dynamic access remain unknown, so renaming requires review. Excluded files (including maintainer scripts), unselected packages and external consumers are unassessed, not proven absent; usage_scope records the configured analysis boundary. Public attributes of classes explicitly exported through __all__ or public package-facade bindings are treated as supported API and retained, including aliased re-export chains.

**Problem**
```python
class Worker:
    def __init__(self):
        self.pending = []
    def run(self):
        self.pending.clear()
# tests/test_worker.py
from app.worker import Worker
def test_run():
    worker = Worker()
    worker.run()
    assert worker.pending == []
```

**Preferred**
```python
class Worker:
    def __init__(self):
        self._pending = []
    def run(self):
        self._pending.clear()
        return 'done'
# tests/test_worker.py
from app.worker import Worker
def test_run():
    assert Worker().run() == 'done'
```

Review whether the attribute belongs to the supported API. For internal state, add a leading underscore, update class references and test observable public behavior. Keep deliberate external or framework contracts with a reasoned suppression. Suggested names avoid observed collisions; no automatic rename is performed.

Run `smelt explain test-only-public-attribute` for details.

nondeterministic-test-data.title: SMT431: A test module calls a known random or time-derived data generator.
nondeterministic-test-data.description: A test module calls a known random or time-derived data generator. Fixed IDs and values keep ordinary test setup reproducible and make failures easier to replay. This opt-in review recognizes direct uuid1/uuid4, os.urandom, secrets and common module-level random calls, including resolved import aliases and fixture/helper bodies in analyzed test modules. It groups calls on one source line. It does not infer whether randomness is the behavior under test. Seeded Random instances and unknown generators are outside scope; module-level random calls are reviewed even if a seed was set elsewhere. Production source and test-quality exclusions are not checked. Repair: Use fixed inputs such as UUID(int=1), or an explicitly seeded local random.Random(seed) when generated variation matters. Keep tests of randomness, entropy and unique-ID behavior with a reasoned suppression. Preserve falsy-ID regression scenarios; change only incidental random setup. No source is rewritten. Enable rules: {nondeterministic-test-data: warning} or select SMT431.
nondeterministic-test-data.markdownDescription:
**SMT431 — nondeterministic-test-data**

A test module calls a known random or time-derived data generator.

Fixed IDs and values keep ordinary test setup reproducible and make failures easier to replay. This opt-in review recognizes direct uuid1/uuid4, os.urandom, secrets and common module-level random calls, including resolved import aliases and fixture/helper bodies in analyzed test modules. It groups calls on one source line. It does not infer whether randomness is the behavior under test. Seeded Random instances and unknown generators are outside scope; module-level random calls are reviewed even if a seed was set elsewhere. Production source and test-quality exclusions are not checked.

**Problem**
```python
from uuid import uuid4

def test_create():
    lease = create(uuid4(), uuid4())
    assert lease.active
```

**Preferred**
```python
from uuid import UUID

def test_create():
    lease = create(UUID(int=1), UUID(int=2))
    assert lease.active
```

Use fixed inputs such as UUID(int=1), or an explicitly seeded local random.Random(seed) when generated variation matters. Keep tests of randomness, entropy and unique-ID behavior with a reasoned suppression. Preserve falsy-ID regression scenarios; change only incidental random setup. No source is rewritten. Enable rules: {nondeterministic-test-data: warning} or select SMT431.

Run `smelt explain nondeterministic-test-data` for details.

unused-suppression.description: An inline suppression is unused or names an unknown identifier. Unknown identifiers, including rule names instead of SMT codes, are diagnosed even in narrowed checks when SMT901 is selected. Known inactive rules are not treated as unknown. information-hiding.title: information-hiding: Keep implementation details private, including APIs exposed only for tests.
information-hiding.description: Keep implementation details private, including APIs exposed only for tests. Review unnecessarily public functions, methods, module constants/type aliases and data attributes. Test-only consumers do not justify public visibility; the current test-only reviews cover module functions and data attributes. Methods with observed test users retain SMT316's external-use exclusion. Each diagnostic retains its own evidence, conservative exclusions and stable SMT code. This selection does not include moving private class constants (SMT334) or extracting static helpers (SMT317): those are placement conventions. A group severity supplies the default for its members; explicit individual settings in the same map override it regardless of key order. Closest-package overrides still win. Existing individual names, suppressions and debt identities remain valid. Members: SMT316, SMT320, SMT335, SMT429, SMT430.

^SMT101$.title: SMT101: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.
^SMT101$.description: A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist. Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.imports.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain. Repair: Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.
^SMT101$.markdownDescription:
**SMT101 — layer-boundary**

A layer imports a layer outside its `may_depend_on` allowlist.

Layers only stay replaceable and testable when dependencies point in one direction. An application service that imports infrastructure cannot be used without the database, HTTP client or framework behind it. With architecture.imports.transitive, the allowlist also applies to every reachable layer, including paths through allowed layers and helpers. Indirect findings include a shortest import chain.

**Problem**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import SqlVoiceSessionRepository
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/session.py
from gateway.features.voice.application.ports import VoiceSessionRepository

# gateway/bootstrap.py wires SqlVoiceSessionRepository to the port
```

Depend on an abstraction (a port) owned by the importing layer or an allowed layer, and wire the concrete implementation in the composition root.

Run `smelt explain layer-boundary` for details.

^SMT102$.title: SMT102: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.
^SMT102$.description: A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs. Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.imports.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence. Repair: Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.
^SMT102$.markdownDescription:
**SMT102 — cross-feature-import**

A feature imports another feature outside the allowed layer pairs.

Features are independent slices. Direct imports between them couple release cycles and make it impossible to reason about one feature in isolation. With architecture.imports.transitive, allowed pairs also apply to all reachable feature modules, with a shortest import chain as evidence.

**Problem**
```python

from gateway.features.voice.infra.sql import CallLog
```

**Preferred**
```python
# billing/application/charges.py

```

Go through an allowed relationship, declare an intended one explicitly (`allow: [{from: orders.application, to: billing.application}]`), move the shared concept into a `shared` package, or merge the features.

Run `smelt explain cross-feature-import` for details.

^SMT103$.title: SMT103: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.
^SMT103$.description: A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow. Inner layers should not know about frameworks, drivers or SDKs. Keeping them out makes the core portable and cheap to test. With architecture.imports.transitive, the importing layer's policy also applies to packages reached through project modules, such as domain -> shared.utils -> sqlalchemy. A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed. Repair: Move the code that needs the package into a layer that allows it and expose it through a port, or extend the layer's `third_party` policy.
^SMT103$.markdownDescription:
**SMT103 — third-party-denied**

A layer imports a third-party package its `third_party` policy does not allow.

A shortest chain includes each import's source line. External packages are leaves: their own source is not scanned. Standard-library imports remain allowed.

^SMT104$.title: SMT104: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.
^SMT104$.description: Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules. Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained. Repair: Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.
^SMT104$.markdownDescription:
**SMT104 — import-cycle**

Import cycles between architecture nodes or explicitly selected concrete modules.

Cycles mean two parts can only be understood, tested and changed together. They also cause import-order bugs at runtime, unless one edge is imported only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; such cycles are marked `(type checking only)`. Imports that other rules already forbid (SMT101, SMT102, SMT106) and outbound imports from declared wiring are left out, so a cycle report means the cycle is built entirely from ordinary allowed dependencies. Existing features/layers/siblings scopes aggregate nodes and do not prove a connected concrete runtime module cycle. The opt-in modules scope uses exact resolved modules; its witness prefers runtime edges when a runtime cycle exists. witness_edges records each selected edge's runtime or type-checking phase. Runtime here means outside TYPE_CHECKING, including deferred imports; it does not prove eager import-time failure. type_checking_cycles: ignore excludes annotation edges from cycle analysis while other boundary checks can still include them. Defaults and existing finding identities are retained.

**Problem**
```python
# billing/application/invoices.py
from gateway.features.voice.application import calls
# voice/application/calls.py
from gateway.features.billing.application import invoices
```

**Preferred**
```python
# voice/application/calls.py publishes an event;
# billing/application/invoices.py subscribes to it.
```

Break one edge of the cycle: extract the shared piece into a module both can import, invert one dependency behind an abstraction, or merge the parts.

Run `smelt explain import-cycle` for details.

^SMT107$.title: SMT107: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module.
^SMT107$.description: Code outside a contracted package imports a private implementation module. Explicit entry points keep callers coupled to a package's supported interface. Internal imports and intentional symbol re-exports through public facades remain valid. Wiring and composition roots still obey these contracts. Layer and feature policies apply independently. Repair: Import through one of the contract's public entry points. Expose a deliberate API there if needed, or explicitly revise the contract. Public entries are exact module patterns; add .** only when the whole subtree is intentionally public.

```python
from app.orders.storage import OrderStore
```

**Preferred**
